steps.name: fast-q01
steps.articleText:
Fast answer

What does Paws do with work items that were in flight when the process starts up again?

Paws recovers in-flight work instead of restarting it from scratch. After startup it examines resumable work items and, when a runner still holds the work, resumes it in a fresh Paws session and reattaches to the same command; an in-progress Closeout verification is instead re-verified and attached to the runner’s existing review. (src/db/recovery.ts:57-86) (src/core/recovery.ts:97-105) The documented behavior is that runners keep working while Paws is down and Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks. (README.md:52-55)

Merging has a special safety path: an item in the merge queue keeps its queue position, and if its GitHub merge call may have been in flight, Paws asks GitHub whether that call succeeded before proceeding. This is detected from the durable merge_call record. (src/db/recovery.ts:65-74) (src/core/recovery.ts:75-82) (src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80) If a run was still active, Paws re-verifies rather than blindly resuming it. (src/core/recovery.ts:79-82) (src/core/recovery.ts:94-97)

Items with an existing capacity-wait, pending answer, or pending transient retry are left alone because their next attempt is already scheduled; other items may be resumed, re-verified, or asked in Linear whether to start again. (src/db/recovery.ts:58-65) (src/core/recovery.ts:101-105)

steps.name: deep-q01
steps.articleText:
Deep answer

What does Paws do with work items that were in flight when the process starts up again?

Paws treats startup as recovery rather than abandoning in-flight work. On startup it examines work items in awaiting_input, running, verifying, recovering, and merge_queue, then chooses a per-item recovery action. (src/db/recovery.ts:46-74) (src/db/recovery.ts:31-37)

Normally, an interrupted running or recovering item is resumed once in a fresh agent session, from its checkpoint when available; without a checkpoint it resumes from its branch. If the remote runner still holds the work, Paws resumes with reattachment to that existing command instead of starting over. A verification whose runner still holds the Closeout review or check run is re-verified and attached to that work. (src/core/recovery.ts:75-105) The README says runners keep working while Paws is down and that Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks. (README.md:52-55)

Merge-queue items normally keep their queue position. If the GitHub merge call may have been in flight when Paws stopped, the merge job first asks GitHub whether the merge went through before moving the item. (src/db/recovery.ts:41-44) (src/core/recovery.ts:75-82) The in-flight condition is recorded durably in the merge_call table. (src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80) If the underlying run was still active, however, the item is re-verified rather than merely kept in place. (src/core/recovery.ts:94-97) (src/core/recovery.test.ts:122-141)

There are safeguards against repeatedly restarting the same work. An item that has already been resumed during the current recovery cycle is generally put on hold and Paws asks in Linear whether to start it again; the item remains in recovering until the question is answered, and repeated startups preserve the hold and the single runnable question. (src/core/recovery.ts:101-105) (src/core/recovery.test.ts:82-109) (test/restart-ask.test.ts:181-207) (test/restart-hold.test.ts:97-131) Startup also skips items whose follow-up is already scheduled: items parked for capacity, items with a pending answer resume, and items awaiting a transient retry. (src/db/recovery.ts:62-64) (src/db/recovery.ts:103-113)

For items waiting for input, startup releases the associated run capacity and queues a catch-up job for open questions. (src/db/recovery.ts:89-98) The startup recovery and its database transition/job updates are committed together in one transaction, and newly scheduled resumes are staggered five seconds apart. (src/db/recovery.ts:51-86) (src/db/decisions.ts:17-26) The startup-resume test shows that items left in recovering by shutdown are passed to recoverOnStartup, after which resume work is claimed and the implementations are run again. (test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts:143-177)

steps.name: fast-q09-rationale
steps.articleText:
Fast answer

Why does Paws wait five seconds between resuming tasks after a restart instead of resuming them all at once?

Paws staggers restart resumes by assigning each resume job a progressively later runAt time rather than scheduling every eligible task immediately. In recoverOnStartup, nextResumeAt() computes now + STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS * resumes, and each eligible resume decision receives that timestamp when its job is applied (src/db/recovery.ts:51-87). This suggests the spacing is intended to avoid a restart surge by spreading recovered work across time, but the examined code and documentation do not explicitly state that rationale.

Not every startup item is delayed this way: items requiring a restart question are excluded; items already parked for capacity, awaiting an answer, or awaiting a transient retry are skipped; and some re-verification work is attached to existing runner closeout rather than receiving a new resume time (src/db/recovery.ts:57-86). Pending answer-resume and transient-retry jobs are also recognized as existing recovery work (src/db/recovery.ts:116-147).
